text: I retain the raw inputs unchanged and record each cleaning step in order. Exact duplicate exported rows are removed to prevent double-counting. Negative-quantity rows are return events: I keep them separately and subtract their value instead of treating them as errors or new sales. Imported appliances were entered in USD, so I multiply their unit price by the documented 3780 UGX per USD; other categories are already UGX. Percentage discounts above one are divided by 100 to obtain fractions. Slash dates mean day/month/year; I standardise them to ISO without shifting an order to another month. Walk-in orders with missing customer IDs stay in the sales population; I use the supplied 1999-to-1007 alias and do not invent identities. For the clean-table report I compare the same 2025 delivered-order rep/month population to SQL, checking gross, returned and net amounts within 1 UGX after rounding. The raw USD prices were rounded to cents and cannot exactly recover the original UGX amounts; I explain that residual rather than overwrite results to match SQL. Required inputs are orders_raw.csv, order_items_raw.csv, customers_raw.csv, products.csv, reps.csv and riverside.db.
